title: Freshman Mixer
description: This party is exclusively for our VIPs, the Class of 2030! We'll have DJs, lights, snacks and lots of fun. It is a lock-in event so once you are dropped off you can't leave, but you won't want to anyhow! Casual attire is fine! You need your digital ID to enter.

title: Open House Night Two
description:
During the Open House evenings, you will have the opportunity to meet your student's teachers, learn about the curriculum in the courses your student is taking, and experience many of the resources we offer to students and families of Stevenson High School. 
 


Open House is scheduled for two nights, one of which parents should attend based on their last name. If you have a calendar conflict with the designated Open House evening, please feel free to attend on the other date. There is no need to inform us of the change. We encourage all parents to attend one of the two nights.


 Thursday, September 3, from 7-9:30 p.m.: Last Names M - Z

title: Honors Senior Solo Recital
description: The  finest senior performers  in our music department will be performing major solo works! These musicians were selected from a panel of judges to perform for this event. Those who cannot attend the event can  stream the performance .

title: Family Engagement: The Opposite of Happiness
description: George Loewenstein, Ph.D., will be in conversation with Eli Finkel, Ph.D. (FAN '17), a professor at Northwestern University, about his new book: "The Opposite of Happiness: How Bad Feelings Make and Break Us."  To register for this webinar, click here .

title: Family Engagement: What To Expect When Your Teen Turns 18
description: Join us on Wednesday, Sept. 23 at 7 p.m. for this event, hosted by Stevenson High School and the Vernon Area Library. Professionals from the Shire Law Group will present what needs to be put in place to protect you and your young adult.

title: Streetfest
description:
Enjoy student performances, participate in wellness activities lead by Stevenson club leaders, a fireworks show, inflatables, and food trucks. Proceeds from Streetfest ticket sales will benefit Shield 23, which serves firefighters in the Lake County area, focusing on financial and peer support for firefighters battling cancer.



General Admission is $10:  Ticketing link

title: CCC - Financial Aid Night
description:
The College Career Center will hold its annual Financial Aid Night at 7 p.m. on Monday, September 28th in the West Auditorium as well as live-streamed via Zoom ( d125-org.zoom.us/j/99298396029 ). This event will be recorded, and the slides and recording will be available on the College Career Center website within a week of the event.

Post Secondary Counselors Ms. Sara Hanson and Mr. Dan Miller will partner with Ms. Maggie Bleeker, Assistant Director of Financial Aid at Northwestern University, to host a Financial Aid Program for families., for this presentation, which is meant primarily for families who have current juniors or seniors.

Details about applying for college financial assistance through the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) will be discussed, along with the types of financial aid available, and how eligibility for aid is determined. Families with seniors typically complete the 2027-28 FAFSA form in October.

title: CCC - First Generation Night One
description:
Please join us for our First Generation to College in the U.S. program on Wednesday, Sept. 30! This information night will be held in-person and is geared toward students who are the first in their family to attend a four-year college or students whose parents have not been educated at the undergraduate level in the United States. While the content is especially helpful for first generation families, all students and families are welcome to attend. Families can select to visit presentations based on their personal needs. These 45-minute sessions are an introduction to topics that will be explained in more detail during future College Career Center events. Families will have an opportunity to ask questions during the live in-person sessions.

 Click here to view our schedule .

title: Fall Choir Concert
location: Stevenson High School | Performing Arts Center
description:
The first choir concert of the year features all three of our curricular choirs, Patriot Singers, Advanced Choir and Stevenson Singers. This concert will feature music from across the world, including Nigeria, Argentina and Ireland, and will explore themes of resilience, love and empowerment. See you there!

description:
Homecoming is back and better than ever this year, thanks to Student Council. Go ahead, and save the date for Oct. 3. Let the planning begin!

title: Fall Play: The Sparrow
description:
Ten years ago, Emily Book, the lone survivor of a horrible school bus accident, was sent away from the tiny town of Spring Farm. Now, in her senior year, Emily must return in order to graduate from high school. Guided by her biology teacher, Mr. Christopher, and befriended by head cheerleader, Jenny, Emily must learn to fit in with her classmates while yearning to stay out of the spotlight. Caught up in a dangerous stunt at a basketball game, Emily reveals her true powers in a stunning display of heroism. Thus, Spring Farm's own darling superhero, "The Sparrow," is born. Can this strange girl with even stranger powers be the hero that her town is longing for, or will her dark secret destroy them all? The Sparrow taps into the fundamental aching of adolescence-fearing that we're somehow different while hoping that we're somehow special.

    

  Production Advisory: Patriot Theatre Company rates The Sparrow PG-13 for mature themes, including grief, bullying, a student-teacher boundary violation, and an instance of gun violence. This production utilizes atmospheric fog and flashing lights.
